expectations: One recall shares a pending row budget between canonical catch-up and effective-event overlays, SQL fetch at most remaining+1 sentinel.
Safe overlay3 with cap2: maintenance-required retryable no context/snapshot; journal/version/job failure budget preserved. cap3 returns all3 references and latest result, canonical stillv1.
Two safe events with2 deltas each share cap3 (reject)/cap4 (complete); not separate per-event budgets.
Unsafe3 cap2 rejects with all pending/job attempts/failures intact; cap3 atomically absorbs all and returns v2 latest state.
Two unsafe targets with1 delta each exceed catch-up cap1: metadata at most2 sentinel, no mass ready marking/claims. cap2 withdelta2 completes both.
Read-before-use runs only selected unsafe event-rewrite jobs; no opportunistic candidate/projection/safe quiet-time jobs.
Actual SQL failure after rewrite rolls back body/absorption but records one real failure; retry retains pending then succeeds under a new finite cycle.
Correction after overflow intentionally invalidates pending and replaces target; deleted target remains inaccessible, no delayed catch-up revives either old view.
CLI over-limit static exit2 with retryable/maintenance_required true and no memory body; scopes always reset.
Standalone background run-jobs remains independently operated; do not claim its total work or full recall byte/graph/SQL work is bounded here.
fixture_size: Separate small tenants: 3-row safe, 2x2 safe, 3-row unsafe, 2x1 unsafe, one fault/recovery, one correction, one deletion. No real model or private input.
retry_semantics: Retain journal; maintenance can catch up separately or a caller can select a larger finite allowance. A limit is not synthesis failure and must not burn failure_count.
